_about: THE VOTE WORDS, written once (the component plan's C3, approved 9 October 2026): what a vote card on a bill's page and a motion's line on a session day say. components.py reads this file and the build writes it into site/components.js, between the WORDBOOK markers, as WORDBOOK.votes. A key starting with '_' is a note and goes to neither.
NOTHING DRAWS THESE YET. The vote cards and the session-day lines take them in the component plan's step 6, shown to the person on real bills first; until then the cards say what they said.

THE RULE, the person's answer of 8 October 2026. (1) The head is the motion's own name in Title Case, then in brackets a short plain gloss in sentence case, with an abbreviation before the gloss only for OTP, OTPA, ITL and IS: 'Inexpedient to Legislate (ITL, Kill the bill)', but 'Lay on the Table (Set the bill aside)'. (2) The chip says what the vote did: 'passed' or 'failed' follows 'Motion Passed' or 'Motion Failed' after a colon, and an empty one is the outcome alone ('Motion Failed'). (3) The chip's colour is the vote's outcome: green where the motion passed, red where it failed, whatever follows the colon. The heads of rows 1 to 6 are the person's, word for word; the other heads are the reviewed draft's as the person's answers revised them, and every chip's words are the reviewed draft's, as the person asked.

A failed motion says 'Motion Failed' and nothing more, except where the failure settled something by itself: Stays on the Table, Earlier Vote Stands, Veto Sustained and Not Introduced. A threshold the motion missed (three fifths, two thirds) is said by the card's threshold note, never by the chip. 'Motion Passed' is the clerk's MA, and 'Motion Failed' both MF and ML; which way a vote went is the clerk's, never the larger number.

{Bill} is the measure's noun ('nouns', by the letters of its number): Bill, Resolution (every resolution and every CACR) or Measure (HA, HCO and HBI). A vote on no bill -- the rules, a ruling of the chair, a reprimand -- never takes one, and says 'Motion Passed' or 'Motion Failed' alone. {Chamber} is the House or the Senate, and {Committee} the committee named (Finance, Ways and Means, Judiciary and so on).

'motion' is null where the head is not one name: a part of a divided question keeps its own motion and names the part ('Adopt the Committee Amendment, Sections 22-24'). A motion to reconsider is 'reconsider' whatever it would reopen, and so is one that tables a reconsideration ('table_motion'). Where the record's words differ from the head by more than case and an amendment number they go on one small line under it, after 'record'.

THE CONSENT CALENDAR (row 33) is one motion and takes one chip. Its bills are listed under 'groups', by what the motion did to each; a group is not a vote and takes no ink of its own. A group whose motion the record marks failed is 'Motion Failed', red, since it records a vote of its own.
A tie fails, since a motion needs more yes than no votes; its note is left out until the House's and the Senate's rules have been read for it (the component plan's step 6).

otp_finance.when: followed the same day by a referral to Finance or to Ways and Means that was not waived; the chamber votes again after that committee, and that later vote is the passage

is.gloss: Study the bill after the session

table_amendment.when: what is laid on the table is an amendment, not the bill
table_amendment.motion: Lay the Amendment on the Table

table_motion.when: what is laid on the table is a motion, such as a reconsideration, not the bill or an amendment; the head names what was tabled
table_motion.motion: Lay the Motion on the Table

floor_amendment.gloss: Change the bill from the floor

amendment.when: whose amendment it is is not stated

nonconcur_conference.motion: Nonconcur and Request a Committee of Conference
nonconcur_conference.gloss: Ask for a conference to settle the differences

accede.motion: Accede to the Request for a Committee of Conference

conference_no_agreement.when: the conferees reported they could not agree

override_first.when: in the chamber that votes first, which does not make the bill law
override_first.gloss: Pass the bill despite the veto; needs two thirds in each chamber

override_second.gloss: Pass the bill despite the veto; needs two thirds in each chamber

postpone.gloss: Kill the bill and bar its subject for the term

rerefer.gloss: Send the bill back to committee

refer.gloss: Send the bill to the {Committee} Committee

vacate_referral.gloss: Move the bill to another committee

waive_referral.when: a referral to Finance waived, which says the opposite of a referral; its head is not settled

recommit.gloss: Send the bill back to committee

special_order.gloss: Take the bill up at a set time

suspend_rules.gloss: Set a rule aside; needs two thirds

order_third_reading.gloss: Send the bill to its final vote

part.when: a part of a divided question, headed by its own motion naming the part

withdraw.when: only where the bill is withdrawn
withdraw.gloss: The sponsor takes the bill back

uphold_ruling.motion: Uphold the Ruling of the Chair

print_debate.gloss: Keep the speeches in the journal

unnamed.when: the record does not name the question: a bare date, a fragment, an empty head
unnamed.motion: A question the record does not name

introduce.gloss: Admit the bill to the chamber

introduce_adopt.when: a resolution brought in and voted at once; it takes row 26's chip

consent.gloss: Decide these bills together without debate
